Appointment may be approved for an additional 1 year extension for a total of 6 years. Position may be eligible for conversion to career-conditional appointments or career appointments. To be converted, the employee must meet all of the following: a) Have been selected for the term position under competitive procedures, with the announcement specifically stating that the individual(s) selected for the term positions(s) may be eligible for conversion to career-conditional or career appointments at a later date; and; b) Have served two years of continuous service in the term positions; and (c) Have been considered to have adequate contributions and a fully successful performance rating for two assessment cycles (including the current assessment cycle) immediately preceding conversion. Service under a modified term appointment immediately prior to permanent appointment shall count toward the probationary period requirements described in 10 USC Section 1599e This position requires you to submit a Confidential Financial Disclosure Report (OGE450) upon entry, and annually thereafter. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS: General education and/or experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: One (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband, NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade, GS-13 or equivalent, in other personnel pay systems including experience in the actual type of work for which application is made. Specialized experience is: Experience identifying communication needs and developing informational materials that inform appropriate and varied audiences of the organization's policies, programs, services and activities. Experience evaluating the effectiveness of information and communication programs in furthering organizational goals. Experience advising senior leaders and management on policy formulation and potential public reaction to proposed policy. Experience with designing and developing informational materials for both the general public and targeted audiences. Experience establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with all media, and internal and external customers. Experience with planning, initiating and implementing comprehensive public affairs and strategic communication campaigns. Experience with advising senior level management on the organization's various communication programs, plans and issues. Experience with application of marketing/partnership principles, methods, and techniques and the ability to apply that knowledge with a high degree of resourcefulness, ingenuity and creativity. Includes the knowledge to segment target markets, identify specific characteristics, and determine the most effective marketing techniques to influence them. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is under the DoD Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo) within Title 5 Competitive Service. For more information on Acq Demo please go to the DoD AcqDemo website at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/ and Fact Sheet at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/faq.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join DAU and be a part of a world-class Department of Defense organization committed to training and supporting Defense acquisition professionals. In addition to training courses, DAU offers a variety of learning events and experiences, provides tools and resources to help on the job, conducts direct assistance to organizations, and offers access to an entire community of practitioners, experts and policy makers. DAU promotes a culture of lifelong learning both for faculty and staff and for the members of the Defense Acquisition Workforce they serve. Join our dynamic team and help give our military the competitive advantage they need.
MajorDuties: Responsible for developing, coordinating, executing, and evaluating an integrated communication strategy and overall program in support of all DAU activities including those of the business units. The program goals consist of an outreach campaign that informs the workforce of product development, activities, services, and capabilities available through the DAU platform. Duties include but are not limited to the following: Works closely with the director of communications and public affairs to plan and organize strategic communication efforts in support of DoD acquisition policy, initiatives and communication strategies as they relate to the DAU mission, its projects, programs and strategies. Helps develop top level messages, themes and products in support of DoD, Undersecretary of Defense (Acquisition and Sustainment) and DAU goals. Provides continual analysis of ongoing outreach initiatives to identify areas for improvement and makes recommendations for adjustment in both short and long range communications planning and programs. Proactively seeks opportunities for extending the reach of communication efforts. Conducts research regarding customer perceptions, defines needs and creates benchmarks to measure success. Identifies emerging issues and targets of opportunity that may arise. Advises senior leaders on metrics development, feedback process management, customer focus, and strategic performance indicators. Works to develop new ways of gathering meaningful input to develop more effective communications strategies and improve understanding of DAU's mission, activities, available products and services, as well as achievements and accomplishments. Serves as a subject matter expert for outreach, communication, marketing, and information sharing, exercising overall responsibility for developing and implementing a comprehensive strategy aimed at communicating the DAU mission and messaging to a variety of federal, military, and commercial audiences. Plans, creates, implements, coordinates, and directs a comprehensive program designed to inform and influence key decision makers in the military, federal and corporate arenas. Informs and trains other personnel in the proper development, implementation, and utilization of market research information, outreach and marketing plans, exhibit design and development, and promotional materials.

Details.RequiredDocuments: You must provide a complete Application Package which includes: Résumé: The latest resume submitted will be used to determine qualifications. Complete Assessment Questionnaire Other Supporting Documents The following documents are required and must be provided with your application. Applicants who do not submit required documentation to determine eligibility and qualifications may be eliminated from consideration. Other documents may be required based on the eligibility/eligibilities you are claiming. They MUST be received by the closing date of the announcement. Online Application: Questionnaire Resume: For qualification determinations your resume must contain hours worked per week (if part-time) and dates of employment (i.e., month/year to month/year or month/year to present). If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as insufficient and you will not receive consideration for this position. If you are a current Federal employee or previous Federal employee, provide your pay plan, series and grade, i.e. GS-0301-09. Current Federal Civilian Employees should list any relevant performance related rating (given within the last three years) and/or incentive awards in your resume. Do NOT include photographs (or links to social media such as LinkedIn), inappropriate material, inappropriate content, nor personal information such as age, gender, religion, social security number, etc., on your resume. Your name MUST be included on your resume. Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD-Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD-Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15. For additional Veteran's information please visit: http://www.usajobs.gov/ei/VetPreference.asp or http://www.fedshirevets.gov Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current DAU employees): You must submit a legible copy of your most recent SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action. Promotion Consideration (Current Federal Employees): If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one year of specialized experience required at next lower grade/band level. You will need to provide additional SF-50s which clearly demonstrates you meet the one year specialized experience requirements (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Promotions, Within Grade, Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s with an effective date more than on year old). ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The Veterans Opportunity to Work (VOW) Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service/discharge and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt. Note: It is the applicant's responsibility to verify that information and documents entered or uploaded are received, legible, and accurate.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Knowledge of logistics, training and travel fields with the Department of Defense or for a major civilian corporation. Ability to communicate concisely, both orally and in writing, to direct, explain, guide, and recommend solutions for a wide range of training and travel requirements and concepts to leadership. Knowledge of support mission requirements in all areas of base support. Familiar with defense travel system (DTS) or equivalent travel or accounting systems to maintain data accuracy and ensure compliance with government regulations. You may qualify at the GS-13, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service: Expert experience in the logistics, training and travel fields with the Department of Defense or for a major civilian corporation. Ability to communicate concisely, both orally and in writing, to direct, explain, guide, and recommend solutions for a wide range of training and travel requirements and concepts to leadership. Expert knowledge of support mission requirements in all areas of base support. Expert Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Skilled in the defense travel system (DTS) or equivalent travel or accounting systems to maintain data accuracy and ensure compliance with government regulations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency provides cross-cutting solutions to enable the DoD, the United States Government, and international partners to DETER strategic attack against the United States and it's allies; PREVENT, reduce, and counter Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and emerging threats; and PREVAIL against WMD-armed adversaries in crisis and conflict
MajorDuties: As a MISSION SUPPORT SPECIALIST (LOGISTICS TRAINING AND TRAVEL) at the GS-0301-12/13 some of your typical work assignments may include: The incumbent works under the supervision of the Support Division for the Chief, Mission Assurance Department (a military O-6) and directly coordinates readiness, mandatory, and professional development training for 80 government and military personnel (GS-13 and above and E-7 through O-6) and 220 contract personnel. Develops training related policies and procedures for the department based upon agency and other guidance. Works with the Training and Integration personnel in developing the department's training standard operating procedure. Assists with the development of the quarterly and annual training agenda. Incumbent directly impacts the capabilities, readiness, and professional competence of the Joint Mission Assurance Assessment (JMAA), Balanced Survivability Assessment (BSA), DoD Red teams and Advance Cyber Assessment Tools (ACAT) by ensuring key scientific and technical personnel are trained on the most current and relevant tactics, techniques, and procedures for their area of expertise. In addition, ensures assessment team personnel are capable of world-wide deployment, including hazardous duty areas. Incumbent ensures assessment and mobile training teams are appropriately equipped to accomplish their mission. Independently develops and manages the organization's training and equipment accountability programs. Establishes criteria and schedules to attain training goals and objectives. Explains the Agency and Department's policy and guidelines to new employees. Assists new employees with registration in the Learning Management System (LMS) and schedules personnel for training courses identified as mandatory for agency employees. Establishes a tracking mechanism to ensure all assigned personnel complete required training. Provides quarterly feedback on training records to the supervisors. Processes approved training requests using the established workflow to ensure timelines are met. Monitors the department's training budget and keeps leadership apprised. Coordinates readiness requirements with the Deployment Readiness Cell. Works closely with the Readiness Cell to coordinate training events conducive to the JMAA Schedule. Ensures personnel complete all required training in order to maintain world-wide deployable. Ensures the department's training plans are consistent with the DTRA's Training and Strategic Plans. The incumbent oversees all aspects of the department's equipment management program, including accountability, issue, receipt, research, and maintenance. Through coordination with assigned equipment custodians, defines the baseline equipment issue for each assigned team. Coordinates equipment issue for new personnel through the Acquisition and Logistics. Ensures military members are outfitted with the proper military uniforms with all accoutrements. Plans for and manages systems, subsystems, and equipment throughout their life cycle, including integrated logistics support activities. Develops, initiates, integrates, and manages all logistics actions associated with life cycle management of equipment. Serves as logistics focal point throughout the system's life cycle. Formulates logistics management and fiscal policy for division high value equipment. Analyzes the demand for supplies and forecasts future needs to ensure adequate supplies and equipment are on-hand to support mission needs. Manages the inspection, shipping, handling, and packaging of supplies and equipment to include return of defective equipment for repair. Establishes and monitors warranties on high value items. Evaluates bids and proposals submitted by potential suppliers and recommends the best product that meets the division's needs and is the most cost effective. Maintains accountability for supplies and equipment. Resolves problems related to storage, safety, and other hazards. Manages storage space utilization and develops and maintains a storage facility to include maintenance, future upgrades, and working stock requirements. Schedules and coordinates movement of equipment by commercial or military modes when required. Makes travel arrangements for deploying team members, including military airlift, if required; coordinates passport requirements through coordination with U.S. State Department and Embassies, billeting, ground transportation, country/theatre clearances, and coordinates any assessment-specific requirements. Prepares operations orders/travel authorizations for each deployment of division personnel to conduct assessments or training. The incumbent assumes a leadership role in establishing criterion for the department's mission specialists and enacts policies/procedures to accomplish established objectives. Reviews applicants for mission support specialists' vacancies within the department, provides prioritized selection, conducts interviews.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Quality and Technical Analyst your resume and supporting documentation must support: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-13 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. To qualify at the GS-14 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: GS-13: Demonstrating comprehensive and expert knowledge of technical and quality processes related to organizational relationships, standards, principals, regulations, precedents, and new developments. Analyzing techniques and evaluating methods to investigate and research issues, which lead to the development of effective and efficient Technical and Quality solutions. Monitoring end user compliance with policies affecting/involving functional areas. Providing guidance and advice to operating or management officials on policy/procedures interpretation. GS-14: Applying quality assurance (QA) concepts, operating principles and methodology applicable to major agency QA programs and mission areas. Analyzing and resolving very complex or sensitive problems related to quality assurance, and in applying new developments and methodologies to the TQ process and program areas. Ensuring processes are in compliance with applicable laws/policies/regulations, well documented and regularly maintained (e.g., process system memorandum, functional system specifications, Standard Operating Procedures, and process-related training). Extensive work on DAWIA certification, DLA TQ training, processes and procedures compliance on applicable platforms. Planning, implementing, and overseeing audit evaluation for managed programs to include providing expertise on process and system for End-to-End process reviews, risks, and controls. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: America's Combat Logistics Support Agency: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) agency. DLA provides worldwide logistics support for the missions of the Military Departments and the Unified Combatant Commands under conditions of peace and war. It also provides logistics support to other DoD Components and certain Federal agencies, foreign governments, international organizations, and others as authorized.

Serves as the program manager for Technical and Quality (TQ) Workforce Development, Acquisition Workforce Engineering and Technical Management (ETM) and Test and Evaluation T/E Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) certifications.

Responsible as the senior advisor to the Technical/Quality Process Owner regarding enterprise-wide TQ functional process performance issues related to training, DLA audits, DLA policy, records management, 508 compliance and related processes.
Leads and guides the established DLA Sub-Process Owner teams for Acquisition Workforce certifications and Quality/Technical Certification Program (Q/TCP).
Establishes and maintains metrics to monitor business performance for the TQ training portfolio.
Responsible as the senior adviser to the Process Owner regarding completeness and effective communications of divisional guidance stored in the division's SharePoint website.
Analyzes and evaluates Key Performance Indicators, metrics and other process performance critical data to ensure the TQ process area is meeting its performance targets.
Perform all phases of planning, implementing and overseeing audit evaluation for managed programs by providing expertise on process and system for A-123 (E2E review, risk control matrix, etc.).
Serves as lead specialist over TQ processes and systemic issues and problems of particularly high visibility and criticality to the agency.

Conceptualizes in-depth enterprise-wide management studies pertaining to process performance review methodology and procedures to identify problems and develop solutions to improve performance review effectiveness.

Plans, organizes, and directs reviews; assigns segments of the review to various functional process organizations; and coordinates the efforts of the functional analysts/experts throughout the agency.
Coordinate?s findings, provides agency expertise in the development of supplemental guidance for enterprise-wide implementation, and evaluates its impact/effectiveness on TQ functional processes.

Reviews and interprets new or changing policies and procedures, determines their impact on existing/envisioned TQ functions, develops and/or challenges concepts, and provides justification when dealing with precedent setting or problem situations.
Coordinates on behalf of division leadership reporting and internal communications to include TMTs, SITSUMs, and any other specialized request from senior leadership on specific TQ activities.

DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) has established a Drug-Free Federal Workplace Policy. All applicants tentatively selected for DLA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Applicants who refuse to be tested will be denied employment with DLA for a period of six months. This policy extends to random testing for the use of illegal drugs by employees who occupy testing designated positions defined as sensitive in Section 7(d) of Executive Order 12564. The Defense Logistics Agency's Drug Free Workplace Plan's drug testing panel includes testing for the following illegal substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates (codeine/morphine), 6-Acetylmorphine (heroin), phencyclidine, amphetamines (amphetamine/methamphetamine), methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), oxycodone, oxymorphone, hydrocodone, and hydromorphone. ADVISORY: By using cannabidiol (CBD) products you are risking a positive drug test result for marijuana.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes (1) Planning, developing, coordinating, and/or scheduling organization's activities; (2) Ensuring content of organization courses accurately reflects current and future policies, capabilities and equipment; (3) Participating in planning projects, programs,' and/or working groups to develop and evaluate training. Knowledge of USAF doctrine and employment sufficient to advise Sr Army Officers and instruct Jr Army Officers and Sr NCOs on USAF employment. Knowledge of the US Army doctrine and employment sufficient to work independently and identify doctrinal conflicts between the USAF and US Army. Ability to design instructional programs, maintain currency in the program area, and incorporate modification to curricula abased on relevant evaluation data. Ability to effectively instruct adult learners in USAF doctrine, organization, equipment, tactics, techniques, and procedures. Ability to coordinate, manage, and schedule multiple USAF courses in a rapidly changing academic environment. Skilled in the utilization of computers, word possessing, power point, and audio-visual equipment in the performance of classroom instruction. Skill in tactfully and efficiently communicating USAF doctrine and employment to Army audiences, including senior officers and their staffs. Skill in communicating in writing, in order to write reports, lesson plans, edit doctrinal publications, provide after action reports and lessons learned. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience GS-09: One year of specialized experience which includes applying analytical and evaluative techniques in the identification, consideration, and resolution of administrative/program issues or problems of a procedural or factual nature. Plan and organize work, and experience demonstrating verbal and written communications to prepare reports, policy statements and guidance, implementation plans, and presentations. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Management OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience GS-11: One year of specialized experience which includes conducting studies utilizing studies and other fact finding techniques in order to develop recommendations to improve aspects of the program; preparing and delivering briefings to managers regarding study findings in order to recommend changes in the program; analyzing documents such as policies, procedures, directives and reports in order to identify and assess potential impacts to the program. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Management, etc. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is for a Operations and Training Specialist at Fort Benning, Georgia located within the Martin Army Community Hospital. Martin Army Community Hospital (MACH) was opened in 1958 and is named in honor of the late Major General Joseph I Martin. MACH, a major subordinate command of the U.S. Army Medical Command, furnishes medical care to an eligible patient population in excess of 72,000 beneficiaries. Conveniently located off I-185 and Marne Road.
Details.SubAgencyName: Martin Army Community Hospital, Operations and Training Division, Readiness Branch
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Benning is located in the "Tri-Community" comprised of Columbus, GA; Ft. Benning, GA; and Phenix City, AL. Columbus (Georgia's third-largest city) is home to the 15-mile trail known as the Chattahoochee RiverWalk. The RiverWalk provides an excellent facility to bike, in-line skate, jog, or just take a leisurely stroll and enjoy the scenery. Columbus offers a variety of attractions such as the State Theatre of Georgia, the historic Springer Opera House; the National Civil War Naval Museum at Port Columbus; the National Infantry Museum, which displays a large collection of military art and artifacts; the Columbus Museum, one of the largest state-of-the-art facilities in the Southeast; and the beautiful Historic District - circa 1850-1870. The stunning Florida gulf shores and Blue Ridge Mountains are only a few hours' drive. For more information, please visit http://www.army.mil/info/organization/benning/

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Interchange Agreement Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes administering Emergency Relief services by making available loans, grants and referrals to authorized personnel, planning, managing, researching, analyzing, and interacting effectively with the public. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Attention to Detail Customer Service (Clerical/Technical) Leadership Oral Communication Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-09).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as the Lead Army Emergency Relief Specialist, Army Community Services, Morale Welfare and Recreation representing the installation in the Army Emergency Relief (AER) program.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. About Fort Bliss: Fort Bliss supports over 30,000 troops, and has undergone the largest post expansion in the Army. It is the home of the 1st Armored Division, FORSCOM deployable units, and has a full scope of base support elements. It is home to the U.S. Army Sergeant's Major Academy, William Beaumont Army Hospital, 32nd Army Air and Missile Defense Command, Brigade Modernization Command, and Joint Task Force North. Ft Bliss plays a vital role in America's largest city on a U.S. International Border, El Paso, Texas. El Paso's climate is dry/sunny with mild winters and warm summers. Web Site: https://home.army.mil/bliss/
MajorDuties: Provides specialized program knowledge in administering Army Emergency Relief (AER) services by making available loans, grants and referrals to authorized personnel.
Administers the Army Emergency Relief (AER) program which provides financial assistance to members of the military and dependents with various types of service-connected emergency situations.
Ensures policies are in place for Army personnel retiring, separating, or being eliminated from service to clear the installation through Army Emergency Relief (AER) office.
Regularly prepares and maintains Army Emergency Relief (AER) records.
Responsible for assuring that the work of the Army Emergency Relief program is carried out by performing a range of coordinating and supportive duties and responsibilities.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The foundation for success of the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) mission is our people. We have a workforce of more than 13,000, reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4 billion. We take pride in offering a valued benefit that contributes to military family readiness and enhances quality of life by providing a service that almost all military families use. As one of the few international grocery chains, we operate 236 commissaries throughout the world. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Serves as the Store Associate in a Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) location. The primary purpose of this position is to performs regular duties within their assigned area of responsibility in the Commissary. Employee can be rotated throughout the commissary (Front End, Grocery, etc.) to perform duties. Position responsibilities include: Assist customers answering questions such as item price or location and handling bulky/heavy items. Operate an electronic checkout system to record unit price, total customer purchase and make correct change. Perform a variety of duties in handling, preparing, and maintaining stock levels of grocery and produce items. Review stock levels and gather inventory data in order to maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system. Prepare and maintain a variety of documents to order commissary items, reconcile invoices and submit requisitions. Maintain security, safety and sanitation practices and procedures.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Provide daily oversight of unit operations
Prepare/reviews correspondence for substance and accuracy
Manage the unit personnel and medical readiness programs
Responsible for the unit supply and logistics programs
Manage all aspects of facility maintenance, contract oversight, and staff coordination
Managing various types of financial management programs
Provide advice on pay, benefits, and entitlements processes and procedures
Participate in management of unit and individual training
Assist in the development and implementation of unit training plans and schedules
Process Personnel Actions
Details.Education: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management and Organizational Design and Development. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Challenge Yourself - Be an Army Civilian - Go Army! Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is located at Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico and is part of the Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (DFMWR). The Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (DFMWR) mission is to create and maintain "FIRST CHOICE" MWR products and services for America's Army, essential to a ready, self-reliant force Fort Buchanan is located adjacent to the city of Guaynabo and is approximately 4 miles from San Juan. The temperature does not vary very much as it is located in a torrid zone. The island of Puerto Rico is an U.S. territory and there are approximately 3 million habitants. Year round warm weather and constant warm breezes and access to beaches makes Puerto Rico a prime choice for vacationers.
MajorDuties: Through subordinate activity managers, is responsible for overall management and direction of the DFMWR Business and Recreation Division at a large garrison.
Coordinates with Garrison Directorates and Tenant organizations to facilitate and promote DFMWR programming and services.
Responsible for overall management of fiscal resources of the DFMWR Business and Recreation Division.
Provides leadership and supervision and communicates mission and organization goals to subordinates.

Directs, develops and administers plans and procedures. Implements, enforces, and ensures compliance with regulations to provide aggressive community business program, and a comprehensive community recreation program.

Provides sound leadership and supervision to ensure attainment of the established objectives of the division. Provides policies and guidance to ensure attainment of the established objectives of the divisions.
Reviews program objectives and priorities and develops five-year plan with Capitol Purchase Minor Construction (CPMC) and Annual Operating Budgets covering projected programs of division resources.
Develops and/or recommends methods, operations, and programs to ensure profitable business activities income.
Institutes innovative programs to meet future needs, including development and support of contingency operations.
Develops policy and strategic plans addressing resources, facilities, and programs.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Perform one or more of the following assignments: manage unit and individual training; manage unit personnel and medical readiness programs; manage unit supply and logistics programs and/or manage various types of financial management programs.
Serve as the military personnel technical expert for the unit.
Coordinate, monitor and evaluate significant projects and activities concerning Headquarters and Command-wide administrative issues.
Advise leadership and other staff regarding administrative matters.
Review military, administrative and personnel related correspondence to make determination on adequacy prior to submission to higher headquarters.
Provide training and technical guidance for administrative activities and personnel within the organization.
Coordinate resources for assigned programs and training events.
Evaluate administrative issues to recommend actions or develop policy to improve administrative operations.
Utilize various automation programs concerning information on readiness that impacts individual service members and the unit?s overall mission or deployment readiness status.

MajorDuties: Assists in the management of a large, high volume, Name Brand Casual Dining (NBCD) franchise restaurant. Assists in the oversight of all restaurant systems and is responsible for purchasing, receiving, preparation, and presentation of all products in a timely manner and according to established recipes and procedures. Ensures consistency in food and service to increase sales. Maintains budgeted food and service labor costs and proper inventories. Formulates instructions and gives direction necessary to operate a fluid, and efficient food production operation. Ensures proper handling, maintenance and storage of all items. As a second level supervisor, reviews the actions of subordinate supervisors and employees. Conducts management review of patron food production programs to identify problems and initiate appropriate corrective measures. Evaluates the success of programs in terms of profitability, customer satisfaction and mission accomplishment. Monitors the procurement of all supplies and equipment for the activity.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located at: 200th Military Police Command, 308th Military Police Company, 535th Military Police Battalion, 11th Military Police Brigade, Fort Carson, CO. Description of working environment: Work is performed in an office setting. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Provide daily oversight of unit operations
Prepare/reviews correspondence for substance and accuracy
Manage the unit personnel and medical readiness programs
Responsible for the unit supply and logistics programs
Manage all aspects of facility maintenance, contract oversight, and staff coordination
Managing various types of financial management programs
Provide advice on pay, benefits, and entitlements processes and procedures
Participate in management of unit and individual training
Assist in the development and implementation of unit training plans and schedules
Process Personnel Actions
Details.Education: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management and Organizational Design and Development. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. FOREIGN EDUCATION: If you are using education completed in foreign colleges or universities to meet the qualification requirements, you must show the education credentials have been evaluated by a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign education programs and such education has been deemed equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program; or full credit has been given for the courses at a U.S. accredited college or university. For further information, visit: http://www.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ous/international/usnei/us/edlite-visitus-forrecog.html.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a military technician position with the 335th Signal Command (Theater), Detachment 3, Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) located at Fort Carson, CO. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manage the daily operations of a US Army Reserve unit?s mission readiness program.
Represent the US Army Reserve Troop Program Unit Commander in his/her absence.
Perform as the record manager.
Serve as the unit physical security coordinator.
Review regulations and directives and implements changes in appropriate manner.
Compile data and create products to present at briefings.
Prepare and review command correspondence for content and accuracy.
Manage unit and individual personnel and medical readiness.
Execute the unit's supply and logistics program.
Coordinate the management of unit and individual training readiness.
Administer financial management program including Government Purchasing and Travel Card programs.
Advise on pay, benefits, entitlements, incentives, and assist with correcting pay issues.
Details.Education: Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related, in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management, and Organizational Design and Development. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a TITLE 32 RANGE OPERATIONS MANAGER (MI FCTC), Position Description Number D1130000 and is part of the MI FCTC, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: ***This is a Title 32 Excepted Service National Guard position which requires military membership*** This position is located in the Joint Force Headquarters-State, Operations Directorate (J-3), Army National Guard (ARNG) Training Center, range Operations. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as a Range Operations Manager with responsibility for live fire training facilities and impact areas; serving as an advisor on all matters pertaining to the use of training center range facilities; and maintaining responsibility for the conduct and safe firing of live ordnance. Manages technicians, AGR personnel, state, contract, and M-Day soldiers. develops state and Federal financial budgets to include the Range and Training Land Program, Integrated Training Area Management program, and state budgets. Plans and coordinates specialized training events involving Active and Reserve Component Special Operations Forces of a classified nature. May support JCS level exercises for Commanders In Chief of Combatant Commands such as U.S. Central Command. 1. Responsible for the timing, coordination, and safety of combined arms firing exercises with involves armed aircraft, maneuvering, mounted and dismounted types of indirect and direct fire. 2. Plans, directs, and managers range activities. 3. Plans and schedules work, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and prepares work schedules. 4. Performs the duties of the director in their absence. 5. Performs other duties as assigned. * The above duty description doesn't contain all details of the official position description. A copy of the entire position description can be found on FASCLASS by searching the position description (PD# D1130000 ). https://acpol2.army.mil/fasclass/search_fs/search_fasclass.asp

MajorDuties: Ensures the facility's Biosurety program remains in compliance with all Federal, State and service regulations.

Develops prudent practices and policies and coordinate the implementation of these policies for customers within the supported facilities, perform inspections and inventories to comply with regulatory guidance and accountability procedures.
Familiarity with regulatory compliance, risk management, systems safety management, biological safety, and safety and occupational health.
Serves as Certifying Official for personnel in the Biological Personnel Reliability Program (BPRP) and is responsible for determining BPRP suitability and reliability.
Ensure that individuals are qualified, trained and proficient to being assigned to BPRP duties.
Incumbent continuously evaluate and monitor personnel assigned in BPRP positions.
Incumbent will promptly remove, or in contracted operations, direct the contractor to remove from BPRP duties, any individual whose reliability becomes suspect.
In such cases, the incumbent will take prompt action to expeditiously resolve the issue and either recertify or decertifying the individual from the BPRP.
Privacy Act considerations according to provisions of the Privacy Act of 1974 apply and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

All personnel being considered assignment to the BPRP must grant authority for release of information and records to allow the incumbent and other authorized officials to review medical, personnel, and security files.

The DJ-02 pay band is equivalent to the GS-05, Step 01 through GS-10, Step 10. For this recruitment, management has decided to at the lower end of the DJ-02 pay band, which is the equivalent of the GS-05, Step 01 to the GS-08, Step 10. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (USAMRAA) is the contracting element of the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command (USAMRDC) and provides support to the Command headquarters and its worldwide network of laboratories and medical research organizations as well as other non-USAMRDC customers. USAMRAA also supports Army-wide projects sponsored by the Army Surgeon General and numerous congressionally mandated programs.
Details.SubAgencyName: U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (USAMRAA)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Fort Detrick is located within the boundaries of the city of Frederick which offers modern housing, schools, recreation areas, excellent utilities, and access to major metropolitan areas. Situated between Baltimore, MD (46 miles), Washington, DC (45 miles), Frederick County, MD adjoins Virginia, West Virginia and Pennsylvania. Fort Detrick is located within the geographic boundaries of Frederick, MD, the second largest city in Maryland. Baltimore, MD & Washington DC are within 50 miles. Real estate and other costs are significantly affected by the close proximity of these two major metropolitan areas. For more information please visit our website at http://www.detrick.healtharmy.mil
MajorDuties: Serve as primary support specialist and office manager to the Command and other U.S. Army Medical Research Acquisition Activity (USAMRAA) senior leaders. Perform a wide variety of administrative and management support functions.
Manage multiple calendars; schedule meetings with internal and external contacts, briefings, and adapt quickly to changes and scheduling conflicts.
Facilitate the preparation and disseminating of personnel memoranda, forms, and reports.
Develop staffing and resource requirements for operational effectiveness and efficiency of administrative and managerial programs.
Apply fact-findings and investigative techniques, and utilize effective oral and written communication in the development of presentations and reports utilizing appropriate regulations.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 80th Training Command, 7th Battalion/98th Regiment, 3rd Brigade, 94th Division located in Fort Devens, Ayer, Massachusetts. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Prepare training briefs and customer support documents.

Details.JobSummary: This position is within the Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) at Fort Drum, Northern New York. FMWR encompasses responsibility for Child and Youth Services, Community Recreation, Business Operations and Support Services. These programs and services enable Soldier readiness and support the resiliency and well-being of Soldiers and Families.
Details.SubAgencyName: Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Drum, home of the 10th Mountain Division (LI), is in northern New York's picturesque North Country, one of the most historically unique and geographically beautiful areas of the United States offering many outdoor recreational opportunities from hunting and fishing to winter sports. Fort Drum is approximately 30 miles south of the Canadian border, 85 miles north of Syracuse, and 350 miles north of New York City. Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) employees enjoy great benefits and unique opportunities including competitive salaries; flexible, part time/full time positions; career diversity and progression; paid leave; medical, dental, vision, life insurance; flexible spending account options and 401K/retirement. FMWR employees are provided job-related training and continued educational opportunities; have access to use free state of the art fitness facilities and a pool; opportunities to work special events to include festivals, 5k runs, and recreational activities while serving our military community; can enjoy Hyper Bowl entertainment, recreational lodging, discounted tickets for theme and local attractions; rent boats, campers, party equipment, etc.; and receive discounted child care while employed by Child and Youth Services (CYS). A career with FMWR awaits you and is your gateway to travel and work at any one of more than 70 U.S. Army installations worldwide. We are excited to welcome you to Team Drum!
MajorDuties: Performs marketing functional services under the general supervision of the Marketing Manager.

Duties include determining marketing techniques and strategies to increase efficiency, enhance participation, and community awareness of key Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation programs.

Conducts Commercial Sponsorship and Advertising. Keeps track of viable annual events for which to seek commercial sponsorship. Packages events, develops solicitation packet and solicits sponsorship from local sponsors.
Negotiates mutually beneficial sponsorship terms and executes all supporting documents.
Coordinates with the installation Staff Judge Advocate to ensure that terms of sponsorship are in accordance with all DA, IMCOM and local regulations and policies.
Attends events and serves as point of contact for sponsors at events. Compile and provide After Action Reports.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) Interchange Agreement Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the education and or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience for the GS-09: One year of specialized experience which includes work such as: 1) preparing office correspondences; 2) managing calendars for organizational leadership; 3) making travel and lodging arrangements; 4) assisting management, administration staff and employees on administrative operations of the office; AND 5) creating and maintaining office files in accordance with established regulations. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. Specialized Experience for the GS-07: One year of specialized experience which includes work such as: 1) preparing office correspondences; 2) managing calendars for organizational leadership; 3) making travel and lodging arrangements; AND 4) creating and maintaining office files in accordance with established regulations. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Superior Academic Achievement: Successful completion of all the requirements for a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement. In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above. Superior Academic Achievement is based on: (1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses, OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR (3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achsnatl.org/). OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Cost Accounting Customer Service Personnel and Human Resources Technical Competence Written Communication Time in Grade Requirement GS09: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the second lower grade or equivalent (GS-07). Time in Grade Requirement GS07: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the second lower grade or equivalent (GS-05).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is an Operations Analyst GS-07 target GS-09 position at US Army Training and Doctrine Command, G-3/5/7, at Fort Eustis, VA. The Deputy Chief of Staff, G-3/5/7 develops, integrates, and manages training operations and requirements, concepts, policies, plans, and directs operations continuously across TRADOC in order to build a campaign capable, expeditionary and versatile Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: As an Operations Analyst working in the Organization Management Division (OMD) G-3-5/7 provides guidance, advice, and technical assistance to management, administrative staff, military, and civilian employees relative to administrative operations.

Responsible for the overall operation and daily functioning of the office.
Participates in identifying and resolving problems arising from internal administrative activities.
Provide weekly reports and feedback to management on personnel action status.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, General Business and Industry Series, 1101 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes working with various organization, state and local procurement laws, regulations, policies, procedures and systems applicable to planning, award, administration and management of contracts; operation of various contract vehicles and the requirements and methods for ensuring compliance factors sufficient to assist in administering contracts and contractor personnel; monitoring contracts and understanding special clauses, terms and conditions to accommodate unique regulatory requirements relative to diverse procurement and federal assistance activities; working with technical requirements and cost and price procedures/techniques to evaluate bids and other information pertinent in the contract administration processes. OR EDUCATION: Applicants must have successfully completed a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of a Contract Performance Evaluator. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of various agency, State and local procurement laws, regulations, policies, procedures and systems applicable to the planning, award, administration and management of contracts is required to effectively interface with the contractor in the administration of contracts for facility maintenance. Skill in and knowledge (demonstrated) of contracts and ability to understand special clauses, terms and conditions to accommodate unique regulatory requirements relative to diverse procurement and federal assistance activities, e.g., entitlement, discretionary grants, and grants to States. Knowledge of technical requirements and cost and price procedures/techniques in order to evaluate bids and other information pertinent in the contract administration processes i volved in the work. Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing. Ability to work effectively with a variety of individuals in the administration of facility maintenance contracts. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is in the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS). Employees occupying DCIPS positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at the ST-IC-W1E8AA USA INTELLIGENCE CTR OF EXCELLENCE. Serve as a Force Management/Manpower Management Analyst; manage military and civilian personnel, equipment requirements and the supporting documentation.
Details.SubAgencyName: US Army Intelligence Center of Excellence; Directorate of Resource Management
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Responsible for staffing, analyzing, and executing force structure actions which impact Intelligence Center of Excellence (ICoE) positions.
Analyze, evaluate and recommend TDA manpower management improvement strategies based on DA Force/Manpower Management guidance and regulations.
Lead analyst for ICoE?s annual Command Plan cycle to include coordinating, training, and documentation.
Conduct in depth, line by line, force management focused, analysis of the TDA looking for errors in MOS/POSCOs, Grade, security coding changes, duplication of effort, and other anomalies.
Finalize by staffing and documenting any identified changes during the CPLAN cycle or in an approved Out of Cycle (OOC) action.
Coordinate across HQ, ICoE and organization to develop Change Management Plans (CMPs) to support leadership?s strategies and initiatives.

State and recommend solutions to Chief, Force/Manpower Management Division regarding anticipated or existing problems in organizational structures and manpower requirements using Army directed Force Management organizational development knowledge.
Utilize force/manpower data management systems to analyze, implement, monitor, administer, and document force/manpower management actions.
Provide advice, guidance and assistance to management on civilian and military force/manpower organization structure and TDA documentation.
Write and staff, as needed, memorandums, EXSUMs, TASKORDs, briefing slides, and emails to / for senior leadership use /review.
Analyze manpower data from a wide variety of source materials, i.e., reports, automated systems, regulatory guidelines, TDAs, manning document, etc.
Review and analyze force management regulations and guidance. Review and track support agreements, MOU, MOA, 7600A between organizations. Process insourcing and AMO packets.
